display.title: Episode 489: The Island of Treasures (Tu B'Av)
display.summary_short: For Tu B'Av, Uncle Yossi urges adding Torah study, then tells of a shipwrecked man made king of an island who spent all its treasure there, not knowing he would one day have to leave.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Tu B'Av. Uncle Yossi explains that the Mishnah calls the fifteenth of Av one of the happiest days for the Jewish people, and that from this day on we add more time to learning Torah, especially at night, through the winter, and encourage friends to do the same. After the Hakochainik march, a ten-year-old girl who visited the Rebbe that day to receive a dollar and a brachah says the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Introducing a lesson from Pirkei Avos, that this world is a hallway before the World to Come, he tells the parable of the island of treasures: a shipwrecked man named Yisroel is crowned king of an island and spends its whole treasury beautifying it, until he learns that a king must leave in rags when the next castaway arrives. He weeps that he sent nothing ahead to his homeland. The island is this world, the treasures are mitzvos, and Torah is the key. The show ends with an invitation to send in compositions and poems, the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to learn from everything we see, a call to sign up friends, the Tzivos Hashem summer spectacular, and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: This world is a hallway to the World to Come: use your time here to store up Torah and mitzvos, the treasures you take with you.
